summary: Tested Emergent Google auth integration (optional sign-in) + My Scans. Backend 10/11 pytest pass: /auth/me (401 unauth, 200 via Bearer & cookie, no _id), /my-scans (401 unauth, per-user isolation, newest first), /predict attaches user_id when authed and null when anonymous, /auth/session bogus -> 401, cookie logout deletes session + clears cookie, CORS echoes origin with credentials=true. Only failure: logout with Bearer header doesn't delete session. Frontend all flows pass: unauth header Sign in + My Scans nav, /history signin prompt, Sign in redirects to https://auth.emergentagent.com/?redirect=<origin>%2Fhistory, bogus #session_id -> error toast + navigate to / (no hang), cookie-auth shows avatar+logout and 'Hello, Test.', empty state then new scan appears in history-list after scan on /, logout restores Sign in and persists after reload. Anonymous scan regression OK with all advice cards, no stale advice-error.

minor.issue: Only reads session_token cookie; Authorization: Bearer token is ignored, so session is not deleted for header-based clients (subsequent /auth/me still 200). Frontend uses cookie so UI unaffected.
No ownership check: anyone with a scan id can read another user's scan (incl. user_id, advice) or overwrite its advice. Consider restricting scans with user_id to owner.

action_items: In /api/auth/logout, fall back to Authorization Bearer token (same as get_optional_user) when cookie missing
Optional: enforce ownership on /api/scans/{id} and /api/advice for scans having a user_id
